hints.title: Partitioned Row Rank Positioning
hints.text: Assign sequential rankings to employees within each company ordered by salary, comparing each rank against half of the company headcount.

hints.title: Window Headcount and Position Range Filter
hints.text: Compute row_number and total company count via window functions. A record qualifies as median when its rank lies between count / 2.0 and count / 2.0 + 1.

hints.title: Median Salary Blueprint
hints.text: With CTE t as (select id, company, salary, row_number() over(partition by company order by salary, id) as rn, count(*) over(partition by company) as cnt from Employee) select id, company, salary from t where rn between cnt / 2.0 and cnt / 2.0 + 1.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
WITH Ranked AS (
    SELECT 
        id,
        company,
        salary,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY company ORDER BY salary, id) AS rn,
        COUNT(*) OVER(PARTITION BY company) AS total_count
    FROM Employee
)
SELECT id, company, salary
FROM Ranked
WHERE rn BETWEEN total_count / 2.0 AND total_count / 2.0 + 1;
```

variables: N: number of records in Employee table
complexity.notes: Window ranking and partitioning sorts rows per company in linear-logarithmic time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Self joins comparing greater and lesser salary counts scale quadratically on large tables.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Window ranking CTE computes median boundaries in a single query pass.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Handling both odd and even headcounts using continuous division boundary conditions.

WITH Ranked AS (
    SELECT 
        id,
        company,
        salary,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY company ORDER BY salary, id) AS rn,
        COUNT(*) OVER(PARTITION BY company) AS total_count
    FROM Employee
)
SELECT id, company, salary
FROM Ranked
WHERE rn BETWEEN total_count / 2.0 AND total_count / 2.0 + 1;

import pandas as pd

def median_employee_salary(employee: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    df = employee.sort_values(by=['company', 'salary', 'id'])
    df['rn'] = df.groupby('company').cumcount() + 1
    df['cnt'] = df.groupby('company')['id'].transform('count')
    median_df = df[(df['rn'] >= df['cnt'] / 2.0) & (df['rn'] <= df['cnt'] / 2.0 + 1)]
    return median_df[['id', 'company', 'salary']]
solutions.approach: Pandas Cumcount and Group Transform Median Filter
